To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DSC-based HiSSTM is a promising model for the analysis of NSC and HPCTM under simulated triaxial loading.
the HiSSD0 model can predict stress-strain response for NSC and HPPC, and DSC-SST 2D computer code can predict volumetric response of HPPC and NSC.

the HiSSD0 model can be used to predict the stress-strain behavior of HPC and the DSC-SST computer program can be used to simulate the stress-strain and volume changes in HPC under CTC and SS conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an advanced numerical modeling technique, which is capable of predicting the behavior of NSC and high performance concrete (HPC).
the development of a constitutive model that can be used to simulate the response of concrete in 3-D loading.
the development and validation of the DSC-based HiS model and its application to simulate the response of NSC, and HPC under 3D stress conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HiSSD0d1 model can be used as an alternative to the DSC-SST computer code to simulate the response of HPC under CTC and SS conditions.
the HiSS models can be used to predict the behavior of HPC and normal strength concrete under simulated loading.
the HiSSD0 model can adequately represent both the stress-strain and volume response of HPC, and the DSC-based HiISS models can simulate stress-strain response under CTC and SS loading conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a single model can be used to represent the behavior of both NSC and HSPC under various loading conditions, and the model constants for NSC and HSC are similar, but the values for the HSC are slightly higher.
the HiSS-DSC-based model and finite element analyses can be used to predict the stress-strain behavior of concrete specimens under simulated 3D loading.
the HiSS-DSC model and DSC-SST-2D code can adequately simulate stress-strain behavior of HPC and NC specimens under simulated 3D loading conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HiSS-DSC model can be used for the analysis of HPC and HSC under 3-D loading conditions.
HiSSD0 model can predict the behavior of NSC and high strength concrete (HSC) under various loading conditions.
DSC-SST and the associated HiSS model can be used for analyzing and predicting behavior of NSC and high strength concrete.
